table.title: Document ingestion environment variables
table.html:
NameRequiredDefaultDescription
DOCUMENT_STORAGE_BUCKET_NAMEYesNoneName of the S3-compatible bucket where uploaded source files and derived page images are stored; the bucket must already exist and be in the same region as the worker fleet.
DATABASE_CONNECTION_POOL_MAX_SIZENo20Maximum number of PostgreSQL connections each API pod may hold; increase only after confirming the PgBouncer pool has sufficient headroom.
OCR_PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_SECONDSNo300Wall-clock limit for a single OCR job before the worker marks the attempt as failed and schedules a retry with exponential backoff.
JWT_SIGNING_KEY_ROTATION_INTERVAL_HOURSNo168Interval between automatic signing-key rotations; retired keys remain accepted for token verification for twice this duration.
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINSNohttps://app.example.comComma-separated list of exact origins permitted to call browser-facing endpoints; wildcard entries are rejected when the service runs in production mode.
FEATURE_FLAG_ENABLE_INCREMENTAL_INDEXINGNofalseEnables delta indexing after document updates; when disabled, a full reindex is required before changes appear in search results.
SMTP_RELAY_HOSTNAMEConditionallocalhostHostname of the outbound mail relay used for invitations and alerts; required when EMAIL_DELIVERY_MODE is set to smtp and ignored when it is set to ses.
table.brief: Environment variables: Name (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE long names) / Required / Default / Description

understanding.purpose: Document the environment variables used to configure document ingestion, including whether each is required, its default, and its meaning.
understanding.reading: Readers scan variable names to find a setting, then read across the row to check its requirement, default, and explanation; they may also compare requirements or defaults down a column.
groups: Name identifies each row and anchors the corresponding configuration details.
Required and Default are compact configuration properties that readers can scan and compare vertically.
Description explains each variable and benefits most from room for natural prose wrapping.
keep_intact: Environment variable names, because they are identifiers readers may copy.
Default values, especially the URL, because they may be copied or interpreted literally.
Required values, including Conditional, so their meaning remains immediately legible.
may_wrap: Description prose can wrap at word boundaries; longer descriptions can use the height created when other cells wrap.
If the table must fit the viewport, identifiers or defaults may need to split, though this makes scanning and copying harder.

preferred.name: r1B
preferred.note: Keep names, requirements, and defaults intact and give prose a more comfortable measure. The table requires 268px of horizontal scrolling, and descriptions begin near the viewport edge.

preferred.name: r3A
preferred.note: Keep names, Required values, and defaults intact, and widen Description for more natural prose wrapping. This accepts more scrolling in exchange for a more readable full table.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Keep all names and defaults intact, but reduce Description from r1B to limit overflow to 212px while retaining more prose width than r1C.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Test a middle ground with more room for names and prose than r1C, while limiting overflow to 170px. Some long names will still wrap, but the URL and Required values stay intact.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Trade some name wrapping for a smaller horizontal overflow while keeping the URL and Required values intact. Description begins earlier in the viewport than in r2C.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Allow some long names to split while keeping defaults and requirements intact. A modest 100px overflow buys a wider description column than the viewport-only design.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Fit within 719px and give Description more room than r1A. Accept breaks in longer names and the URL in exchange for showing every column at once.

bad.name: r3C
bad.note: Fit within 719px and preserve the URL and Required values by moving width from Description to Default. This tests whether intact defaults are worth narrower prose and continued name splits without horizontal scrolling.
bad.why: The narrow description column creates very tall rows and splits a configuration identifier inside the prose. Several row names also break inside words, making the table harder to scan despite fitting the viewport.

rationale: r1B and r3A are identical: they keep the row identifiers and default URL intact while giving descriptions enough width for a manageable row rhythm. Their cost is substantial horizontal scrolling: almost all of Description begins beyond the initial viewport. The narrower alternatives reveal more description initially, but visibly break several identifiers or produce longer rows.

general: Give row identifiers enough width to support scanning and accurate recognition, especially when readers may copy them.
Judge horizontal scrolling against the readability of the entire row and the portion visible on first load.
Allocate prose columns enough width to avoid unnecessarily tall rows and fragmented reading.
specific: The longest environment variable needs about 398px including padding to remain on one line.
A 190px Default column keeps the URL intact, while 99px accommodates Conditional.
The reported split counts do not reflect all visible identifier breaks in the narrower designs.

tradeoffs: r2B fits the viewport and makes the complete row visible at once, but breaks both names and the default URL. r2C and r3B reduce scrolling while preserving the URL, at the cost of broken row names.
uncertain: A designer prioritizing immediate access to descriptions over intact identifiers could reasonably prefer r2B or r3B. The ranges are conservative proportional estimates around the preferred widths, not independently rendered or verified thresholds.

critique.good: Names, requirement values, and defaults remain intact, so the identifying and configuration columns are easy to scan.
critique.problems: Almost the entire description is beyond the initial viewport. Its narrow measure also creates tall rows and large empty areas in the other columns.
critique.cause: The first three columns consume 687px before the 193px description column begins; the table extends 161px beyond the viewport.

critique.good: All four columns are visible at once, and the description has enough width for a reasonably readable prose measure. Required values remain intact.
critique.problems: Several variable names break across lines, sometimes inside a word, and the URL default splits. These breaks make identifiers and literal values harder to scan and copy.
critique.cause: The 260px Name column provides only 239px of text space, while the 150px Default column provides 129px; both are narrower than their longest unbreakable values.

critique.good: Variable names and requirement values stay intact, and the entire table fits in the viewport.
critique.problems: Descriptions form very narrow vertical strips, making rows exceptionally tall and leaving large empty areas across the table. The URL and an identifier in the description also split.
critique.cause: The 398px Name column leaves only 100px for Default and 122px for Description, giving those columns 79px and 101px of text space respectively.

critique.good: The entire table fits in the viewport. Required values and defaults are easy to compare, and the URL remains intact.
critique.problems: Several variable names break across lines, sometimes within a word. Descriptions form narrow, tall blocks, leaving large areas of empty space in the other cells and making rows harder to scan across.
critique.cause: Name has only 216px of text width, while Description has 172px; most of the available width is committed to the first three columns.

critique.good: Names and defaults remain intact, and the wider descriptions make the rows shorter and prose easier to read. The two configuration-property columns remain compact and comparable.
critique.problems: Almost all of Description lies beyond the initial viewport, so readers must scroll to understand a setting and may have to scroll back to reconnect it with its name.
critique.cause: The 398px Name, 99px Required, and 190px Default columns consume 687px before Description begins; the table extends 268px beyond the viewport.

critique.good: It reduces horizontal scrolling compared with r1B while giving descriptions more breathing room than r1A. Required values and defaults remain intact.
critique.problems: Several names break awkwardly, including one with a single letter on its second line. Much of each description still lies beyond the initial viewport, while the prose remains relatively narrow and rows tall.
critique.cause: The 300px Name column is too narrow for several identifiers, and the first three columns total 589px, leaving only about 130px of Description visible initially.

critique.good: Names and defaults stay intact, and the Required column is easy to compare. The shaded first column gives each row a clear anchor.
critique.problems: The description is narrow enough to create tall rows and extensive empty space in the other columns. Almost none of the explanation is visible on first sight, so reading across a row requires substantial horizontal scrolling.
critique.cause: The 398px Name and 190px Default columns preserve their longest values but leave the 245px Description column almost entirely beyond the viewport. The table overflows by 213px.

critique.good: All four headers and complete rows are visible at once. Required values remain intact, and the description has enough width for generally readable prose.
critique.problems: Several variable names break across lines, sometimes inside a word, and the URL also splits. These breaks make identifiers and literal values harder to scan and copy. Long descriptions make the table tall.
critique.cause: The 250px Name column and 150px Default column are narrower than their longest unbreakable values. The 220px Description column also produces several long rows.

critique.good: The wider description improves prose rhythm and reduces table height. Required values and the URL remain intact, and more of the description appears initially than in r2A.
critique.problems: Several long names wrap, including breaks within identifiers despite the reported zero mid-word splits. Much of each explanation still requires horizontal scrolling, and the tall description cells leave empty space alongside short values.
critique.cause: The 340px Name column provides only 319px of text space, less than the longest identifier. The 260px Description column begins near the viewport edge, and the table overflows by 170px.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r3C.why: All columns fit in the viewport, and the required and default values remain intact. Several names split midword, though, and the narrow description column makes rows tall and breaks an identifier.

r2A.why: Names and defaults stay intact, and the descriptions appear to have a more comfortable measure. Almost the entire description column requires horizontal scrolling.

ref_equal.why: The equal column widths leave excessive space in Required while splitting nearly every name, the URL, and a description identifier. The narrow descriptions also make rows tall.

ref_auto.why: Names and defaults remain intact, but descriptions are mostly beyond the viewport and appear narrow enough to create tall rows. Reading each row requires scrolling.

r1B.why: Names and defaults stay intact, and the wider descriptions produce a more compact row rhythm. The description column lies mostly beyond the initial viewport, so reading it requires scrolling.

r2C.why: More of the description is visible initially and the prose has room to breathe, but several names split awkwardly, including a single final letter, while descriptions still require scrolling.

raw.unsure: The supplied images cut off the right side of the scrolling layouts, so the full description widths and exact scrolling distances cannot be judged directly.

ref_equal.why: The table fits the viewport, but equal widths waste space in Required and split nearly every name, the URL, and an identifier in the description.

r2A.why: Names and defaults stay intact, but almost all of the description column lies beyond the viewport, requiring horizontal scrolling to understand each variable.

r3C.why: All four columns fit, Required is compact, and the URL stays intact. Several names and an identifier in the description split, and descriptions wrap heavily.

r1B.why: Names and defaults remain intact and descriptions have room to read after scrolling, but the description column starts almost entirely outside the viewport.

r2C.why: Some names split awkwardly, including a single trailing letter, while most descriptions still require horizontal scrolling. It bears both costs without fully resolving either.

ref_auto.why: Names and defaults remain intact, but descriptions begin at the viewport edge and wrap into tall rows, making the required scrolling especially costly.

raw.unsure: The supplied images cut off the right side of the scrolling layouts, so their full description widths and total scrolling distances are not visible. The choice depends on weighing intact identifiers against seeing complete rows at first sight.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
